LESSON: PLANE GEOMETRY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 2.1: Plane Geometry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Plane Geometry, part of Communication in Pre-Technical Studies in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are combined shapes applied in day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify instruments used in drawing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plane Geometry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain the layout of a drawing environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plane Geometry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. construct combined shapes applied in drawing, embrace the use of plane geometry in drawing.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plane Geometry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify instruments used in drawing,

   Plane Geometry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. explain the layout of a drawing environment,

   Plane Geometry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. construct combined shapes applied in drawing, embrace the use of plane geometry in drawing.

   Plane Geometry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the instruments used in drawing (set squares, drawing set, straight edges and pencils), Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views.

2. use print and digital resources to search for information on setup of drawing paper (drawing surface, margins, title page), Adjust light intensity

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the instruments used in drawing (set squares, drawing set, straight edges and pencils), Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views.
2. use print and digital resources to search for information on setup of drawing paper (drawing surface, margins, title page), Adjust light intensity

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Plane Geometry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: learner acquires team working skills when discussing how to draw combined shapes.

● Learning to learn: learner develops organising skills when using available resources to construct combined shapes.

Values:
● Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions when discussing how to draw combined shapes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: learners work together harmoniously when discussing how to draw combined shapes.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify instruments used in drawing,
2. explain the layout of a drawing environment,
3. construct combined shapes applied in drawing, embrace the use of plane geometry in drawing.

Remember the key question: How are combined shapes applied in day-to-day life?
